evidence.snippet:
## Merged defects

One defect can carry reports from several checks. Every member claim resolves under its own check, rule, severity, and path. Each member gets its own mapping and its own ceiling: the policy is per report. The two caps on a cause read the merged defect instead. A merged defect takes the strongest cause any report proved, with the evidence that proves it, and a `pre-existing` cap or an unproven `affected` cap applies only when that merged cause calls for it. So one report's severity and another's proof combine, as they did before this step, and a merge never lowers what blocks. The cap on an unjudged lens report stays the report's own. The defect takes the strictest result among its members, and the floors then apply to the defect.

Example of the merged cause: one lens reports a P0 on a line nothing ties to the change, and another check reports the same line at P3 as introduced. The defect is an introduced P0 and blocks under the built-in table. Resolved with each report's own cause it would be `advisory`: the P0 capped as pre-existing, the P3 advisory by the table. The answer does not depend on which member speaks for the defect, or on `ruleAliases`. A member here is a report with a finding ID of its own. A lens report whose every claim a verifier refuted is left out, unless every report of the defect is one.

Example: `lens.cleanup` and `static.biome` both report one P1 defect. The root table writes `P1: block`, the cleanup entry sets `ceiling: advisory`, and the Biome entry maps `P1: acknowledge`. The cleanup member resolves `advisory` and the Biome member `acknowledge`. The defect needs an acknowledgement. The cap on a lens finding no verifier judged applies to the lens member alone, never to the Biome member.

## Deterministic checks

Biome, tsc, Enola's rules, and guardrails resolve through the same keys. `static.biome`, `static.tsc`, `static.enola`, and `guardrails` are check names like any lens's. `static.mutation` joins them once step 16 lands, under whatever name it merg [cut at 2 KiB]

explanation.what: A merged finding whose winning sighting is not from `guardrails` loses the guardrails claim whenever that winner carries no `guardrail` match, even though `reportedBy` says the guardrails check also reported it.
explanation.whatToDo: When `reportedBy` contains `guardrails` and no typed match is available, add the whole-guardrail claim regardless of which sighting is `source`; more generally, retain each guardrail sighting's match through merging rather than inferring it from the winner.
explanation.whyHere: The active exact-resolution decision requires every member claim to resolve under its own check and says a guardrail finding without the typed match resolves under its whole guardrail. Filtering guardrails out of `own` and then testing only the winning `source` makes the outcome depend on which sighting won, so a stricter guardrail policy can disappear.

properties.failureScenario: A custom lens and `forbidden-patterns` both report the same added line under rule `guardrail/forbidden-patterns`; the lens reports P1 and the guardrail P2, so the lens sighting wins and the merged finding has `source: lens.custom`, `reportedBy: [guardrails, lens.custom]`, and no `guardrail` field from the losing sighting. With `resolution.checks.lens.custom.P1: silent` and `resolution.checks.guardrails.rules.guardrail/forbidden-patterns.P1: block`, `#claims()` now returns only the lens claim and the finding resolves silent instead of block. This is an unusual but supported same-ID co-report, and the result wrongly depends on the speaker.

snippet.text: The notice resolves under its own check and under the guardrail's, and the stricter result stands. It carries the guardrail match an analyser's configuration notice carries, so resolution reads `resolution.checks.guardrails` and the rule's `analyser` class. It also reads `resolution.checks.static.enola`, since every report resolves under its own check, by [the exact-rule decision](2026-10-17-acknowledge-status-exact-rule.md). So a repository cannot quieten this notice from the guardrails table while its Enola table is stricter, nor from the Enola table while its guardrails table is. The coordinator first answered that it resolve under the guardrails check alone; a round showed that broke the exact-rule decision, and the coordinator then chose both, which never lowers what blocks. Its ID is the guardrail's, which ignores the producing check, so a dismissal matches it as it would the guardrails check's. The policy-change floor keys on the rule and the path, so it treats both alike; a `package.yml` is not a `melian.yaml`, so no floor applies. It is stored under `static.enola`, so a later Enola run replaces it and a guardrails run leaves it alone. `melian findings` shows it with Enola's mark beside the guardrail's rule, since Enola raised it. Stored findings carry no tool text, by [the decision of 2026-11-16](2026-11-16-shared-static-findings-carry-no-tool-text.md): the notice is Melian's fixed sentence and the path.

Its severity is the guardrail's `severity`, not `analyserSeverity`, which blocks a change to an analyser's configuration at P1. This narrows the 2026-10-03 decision that an analyser's configuration change blocks, for these files alone. The ruling made that choice. A Packwerk file is ordinary project structure, which a head adds whenever it adds a package, so a block would stop every pull request that adds one.

## Decision

Each lens's sighting of one ID resolves as its own report, as a report with an ID of its own already does inside a merged defect:

- under its own check, rule, version, and the severity it reported, after any lowering its verifier recorded;
- with its own mapping, its own ceiling, and its own unjudged cap, so a confirmed sighting beside an unjudged one resolves in full;
- leaving out a sighting a verifier refuted while another stands, and counting every sighting when none does.

The finding takes the strictest result, the speaking sighting's on a tie. The floors then apply to the finding, as before.

The two cause caps still read the merged cause: the strongest cause any sighting gave, with its proof, as [the merged defects section](2026-10-17-acknowledge-status-exact-rule.md#merged-defects) sets for reports. Resolving each sighting under its own cause would let a merge lower what blocks. Example: one lens sights an old P0 that nothing ties to the change, and another lens sights the same ID as introduced at P3. Each under its own cause resolves `advisory`; the merged finding is an introduced P0 and blocks. Sightings and reports follow one rule.

The per-sighting severity comes from the claims the findings document already keeps: since step 29, each sighting's claim holds its reported severity in `otherClaims`, beside its own verification. No stored shape changes. A finding that lacks a claim of its own ID for every producer it lists, as one stored before claims kept their severity, resolves every producer at the merged severity, the stricter reading it had before.

## Why

A lens's policy is a statement about that lens's findings. Applying it to another lens's severity, because the two chose the same rule ID, decides one lens's report under another's terms. The same holds for the unjudged cap, which the as-built decision already applies per report.

## What this gives up

explanation.what: The new decision deliberately gives a `static.enola` report the guardrail's finding ID, but it does not amend the active per-sighting decision whose implementation and severity model assume static and guardrail checks never share an ID.
explanation.whatToDo: Either keep the Enola notice under an identity that cannot merge with a guardrails sighting, or explicitly amend the per-sighting decision and retain each static/guardrail sighting's severity and guardrail match so each claim resolves at its own reported values.
explanation.whyHere: When the ordinary guardrails check also reports the path, the pipeline merges the two sightings and retains only the winning severity. Resolution then applies that merged severity to both the Enola and guardrails claims, so it is not actually resolving each report under the severity it reported. The new decision selects its own “resolve under both” criterion while omitting the active decision that governs same-ID sightings.

properties.failureScenario: A repository already lists `packs/**/package.yml` in `policy-change-review.files`. Changing a Packwerk package makes guardrails report the shared ID at `analyserSeverity` P1 and Enola report it at `severity` P2. The merge keeps P1, and `Finding.#claims()` uses that P1 for both claims. With `static.enola: { P1: silent, P2: block }` and the guardrails P1 claim mapped silent, the correct per-sighting result is block from Enola's P2, but the merged finding resolves silent. Reversing those mappings can create a false block instead.

trigger.snippet:
# A head's change to a Packwerk file Enola read draws a policy notice

Amends: [Enola's policy paths come from Enola](2026-11-16-enola-policy-paths-come-from-enola.md), the Packwerk files it leaves to the head
Amends: [Analyser configuration changes](2026-10-03-analyser-configuration-changes.md), a change to a Packwerk file Enola read acknowledges rather than blocks
Amends: [An unresolved acknowledgement fails the status, as built](2026-10-17-acknowledge-status-exact-rule.md), the trigger of a policy notice for a Packwerk file behind a symbolic link

Status: the maintainer ruled on 2026-11-18, on [issue #538](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/538), for the first option there. A head that changes `packwerk.yml` or a `package.yml` gets a policy notice at acknowledge. The head's copies still run. How the notice is raised is the coordinator's answer on approach, given in its session, not a ruling.

Problem: Enola 0.4.40's Packwerk check reads `packwerk.yml` and each package's `package.yml` from the head. A head that sets `enforce_dependencies: false` in a `package.yml` turns the check off for that package, and the review said nothing. The review of record on [pull request #534](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/534) showed it. Replacing the files with the base's copies, as Melian does for Enola's other policy, would judge a head that adds or moves a package by packages it no longer has.

Solution: the Enola check raises `guardrail/policy-change-review` for each Packwerk file Enola read at the base or the head that the head changes, adds, deletes or renames, or that is a symbolic link or lies under one, as Links below says. The notice uses the guardrail's own sentence, "Review the change to `<path>`, which configures Enola's Packwerk check.", at the folder's `guardrails.policy-change-review.severity`, P2 by default, which resolves at acknowledge. A folder that turns `policy-change-review` off draws none. A repository where Enola finds no Packwerk package draws none.
